_about: Parameter table for build_mc39.py. Height datum: footing top (bed plates) to cab floor = the MC-39 standard; eaves = that + 7'6". Base square per standard is IDECO E-4898 table column A (86'3": 20'0 1/4" = 6.1024 m; a straight taper through the table's 79'6" and 99'9" rows gives 20'0" to 20'0 3/4"). Flights 1..n-1 run on the tower diagonal; the top flight runs along one wall to the trap door (USFS T-1004-A cab-landing detail) at the common 12 in 9 1/4 pitch. The only input to the tower build. Lengths in metres unless the key ends in _ft or _in. Design frame: x = east, y = north, z = up; origin at the tower centre on the pad-top plane.
name: MC39_Lookout

standards._about: Cab-floor height, base square (back to back of leg angles) and riser counts per flight, bottom up. USFS T-1002-A and IDECO E-4898.

stairs._layout: USFS T-1004-A and T-1006-A: a 2'-0" stair between 2" stringer angles is 2'-4" overall (marked across the top flight); two of them 6" apart (marked at the 2nd landing) make the 5'-2" landing width, so flight centres are 17" off the diagonal (reading agreed with t-qa; the other reading, two 2'-6" flights 2" apart, gives 16"). Enlarged detail of cab, 1st and 2nd landings: the top landing's inner edge is 2'-1 3/8" from the tower centre line and the next one down 3'-1", along the flight; a flight is n goings between landing edges for n risers.
stairs._top_flight_ruling: team-lead, 2026-10-11: the top flight is 12 rise in 8 run (56.3 deg), per USFS T-1006-A; T1 measures 52 +/- 2 deg on flights 1-7 and 56.3 +/- 2 deg on the top flight; stair width stays 2'-0". No longer pending.
stairs._top_flight: USFS T-1004-A enlarged detail: the top flight runs along one wall from the 1st landing to the cab landing, whose frame stands 9" off the far wall; it scales to 4'-6" of plan for 9 risers, so T-1006-A's '8 in 12' is 8 run in 12 rise (56.3 deg). Its start line meets the end of the last diagonal flight's head edge.

landings._deck: Steel levels are the drawn ones (USFS T-1002-A, the dimension ladder at the left of the elevation, from the top of the tower steel labelled Cab Landing down to Top of Bed Plate): girts, landing frames and the cab-landing frame sit on them. Deck thickness: T-1006-A Typical Landing draws the plank deck on top of the 2 1/2 x 2 1/2 x 3/16 landing angle, with the guard rail 3'-6" approx. up from the deck; the planks are taken as the same 2 in lumber as the treads (read, not printed for the landing; t-qa). INTERPRETATION (t-director ruling/lookout-tower-girt-and-deck-level): the plank's underside lies on the top of the landing angle and that top is on the steel level line, so deck top = steel level + deck_thickness_in.
landings._platform: USFS T-1004-A marks 5'-2" x 2'-6" on the lower landings; the tower faces cut the platform where the corner is smaller.
landings._top_landing: t-director ruling/lookout-tower-top-landing-and-step-off: the top landing fills its drawn frame (T-1004-A enlarged detail): out to both walls, to the line where the top flight starts and to the edge where the last diagonal flight ends. No size is written on the sheet; this outline is derived from elements the sheet places. Disclosed interpretation.

hatch._max_drop: tower-design-spec.md, trap door rule 5: stepping into the open hatch joins flight 8 after a drop of at most 1.3 m. The under_opening record starts where the nosing line is that far below the cab floor.

cab._heights: USFS T-1001-A, Side View of Cab Frame: the dimension chain at the right of the frame reads 3'-6" from the bottom 3 x 3 x 1/4 frame angle (the top of the tower steel) to the sill angle and 4'-0" from there to the eave angle. That view draws the frame only, with no floor surface, so both are taken from the top of the tower steel, not from the walking floor. Read by t-artist from the scan (MPS Fig. 10); tick positions are legible, medium confidence.
cab._collision_inset: the cab wall proxies' inner face stands this far inside the 7'-0" frame plane (the visible wall face is 0.028 m outside it); it sets the collision interior, the walk rectangle and lane 9's walls.
cab._floor: USFS T-1001 (digest mc39-design-r1-1, not read from the sheet by t-qa): double 1 in wood floor with building paper between; the paper's thickness is not modelled. Its underside lies on the top of the tower steel (same interpretation as landings._deck), so the cab's walking surface is that level + floor_thickness_in. lower_wall_ft, window_band_ft and the eaves are measured from the top of the tower steel, not from the walking surface.

pads._stair_foot: INTERPRETATION, not on the sheets (t-qa could not read what the bottom flight rises from): every flight keeps its drawn 9 in risers between walking surfaces, each one deck thickness above its steel level, so the bottom flight starts on a concrete stair landing whose top is one deck thickness above the top of the bed plates. The other reading (foot on the bed-plate level) would make the bottom flight rise 13'-6" + 2".

decay._about: 0 = as built, 1 = worst. Drives rust cover, paint loss, plank splitting and gap jitter. Never removes a member (director note N4).

checks._about: known_findings is owned by t-qa: entries are added or removed only on t-qa's message. A listed check still prints FAIL (known). The build exits non-zero on any unlisted failure, on a listed one that got worse by more than 0.005 m, and on a listed entry that no longer matches a failing check.
checks._body_height: the wall set of a deck (tower-td-note R1b as widened): every collision proxy that lies between wall_slab_floor_clear above the deck's surface and body_height above it, found from the proxy list by a geometric test. body_height is the standing body's (authored controller) height; wall_slab_floor_clear keeps the deck's own floor proxy and a closed trap door out of the wall set.
checks._rail_wall_thickness: every rail-plane wall, flight and landing alike, is a thin box: its face on the visible rail or stringer plane toward the body it restrains, this thickness behind it (t-td ruling 2026-10-11; a proxy stands where something visible stands and never in another body's space).
checks._collinear_tolerance_deg: a junction marked collinear turns less than this and a junction marked bend turns more; the game computes the kind from its own lanes at this tolerance and verifies it against the manifest's mark.
checks._wall_reach: measured by t-engineer's wall-approach probe (TestResults/tower-eng/wall-approach-dt*.txt): a sliding tower capsule's axis rests 0.25 m from a wall; the full-size capsule on the ground, 0.40 m. Used for reach, lip widths, the join envelope and the eye sweeps. Hand-over points, run-out lines and crossings are chosen and stated against capsule_reach.
checks._ground_wall_reach: the full-size capsule (0.40 m) a player has before joining the first lane: where such a body can stand beside the ground end, stated beside the band (which is the tower capsule's, wall_reach) to show every such position is joinable. Not used for the band.
checks._envelope_mouth_guard: regression guard, not a derived bar: at each free end's cross-section the body's centre is at least this far from the nearest edge of any opening on that deck (every stair mouth, the lane's own included; for the exit lane the trap door opening). Set just under the smallest figure when it was introduced (0.2433 m, landing 5). t-td and t-qa, 2026-10-11.
checks._envelope_deck_inset_min: at each free end's cross-section the body's centre is at least this far inside the deck's edge (any edge, stair mouths included). 0.06 m is more than one frame of travel at tower walk speed at 1/30 s (0.053 m), so no single frame on the controller can carry the centre past an edge from where the lane released it. t-td and t-qa, 2026-10-11.
checks._band_tolerance: the one tolerance for the band rules (t-td, 2026-10-11): the no-penetration sweep uses a solid radius of wall_reach less this (0.2495 m; t-qa); rule 4 (band at the lane end against the flight's lip) and the carry across a bend allow this much; the game's build check compares its own accept_at_bend with the manifest's within it.
checks._band_between_samples: how a band is evaluated between two of its 10 mm samples, in the game and here: never wider than computed. Behind a bend, the sample at the bend; elsewhere min(cap, the smaller of the two neighbouring reach samples after the running minimum, lip width + tan(mouth_slope_deg) x distance to the lip or bend).
checks._run_out_rule: t-td, 2026-10-11: no linked run-out turns at the lip. First segment collinear with the flight, at least run_out_first_segment_min; a carried bend is at most carry_bend_max_toward toward the next flight (the lever's own angle, acos 0.82) or carry_bend_max_away away; a stop is at least stop_bend_min (frozen stops) or stop_bend_min_lever (the fallback search). frozen_behaviour is the per-landing behaviour frozen by t-producer and t-director; a landing that cannot keep it is a finding.
checks._run_out_search_time_limit_s: the layout TOOL's time limit per landing, in seconds (a build never searches). Reaching it is 'no result': no block is written, never a partial one.
checks._run_out_final_segment_min: the search's only guard against a degenerate second segment (a bend with almost nothing after it); kept by t-td 2026-10-11.
checks._bend_limit_guard_deg: t-td rule B5a: carry_bend_max_toward is a rounding of the lever's angle (acos 0.82 = 34.9152) and the game decides with the exact lever, so a bend is carried only up to carry_bend_max_toward less this guard and a fallback stop only from stop_bend_min_lever plus it. The game's build check holds its lever within the same 0.01 deg of carry_bend_max_toward. No guard on the 30.00 away ceiling (t-director's) or the 45.00 frozen stop.
checks._amend3: t-director ruling/lookout-tower-upper-landing-step-on-final-amend3 (through t-producer and t-td): a stop fallback only where the bend turns toward the next flight (the ends in stop_fallback_allowed); flight 8 foot, whose bend turns away, has none and takes the shortest first segment that passes instead of the longest; its curve is printed over first_segment_curve [from, to, step]. tower_walk_speed is t-engineer's tuning value, used only to print one frame of travel beside each first segment.
checks._lane_band: the game's laneLateralSlack and laneTaperLength (t-engineer's tuning asset; its reader asserts they are equal): on a flight the lane's band is the lip width at each end easing to lane_lateral_slack over lane_taper_length of slope length.
checks._exit_lane_wall_overlap_max: tower-td-note C6, the named exception: lane 9's line may lie inside capsule_reach of the south wall proxy only, by at most this at its foot, never increasing along the lane.
